messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + SLO targets from today

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before Marcus and I size options: 

Recap (from your side)
- Primary user journey: live search + summarization for customer support transcripts (streaming enabled).
- Latency target: 99th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for short responses (<80 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/minute during business hours, occasional bursts to ~1500 rpm during peak campaigns.
- Concurrency: you expect up to 120 parallel non-streaming requests and roughly 50 concurrent streaming sessions with chunked output.
- Other: strict TLS, ability to pin model versions, and audit logs for query lineage.

Immediate asks from us:
1) Marcus: can you confirm whether the 120 concurrency number is sustained or peak-burst (and how long bursts last)?
2) Legal/Proc: if we get starter commitments we can provide an initial Dedicated pool quote and a short pilot MOA.
3) Ops: we'll propose a connection-pooling and QPS model; see attached "redwood-connection-guidelines.pdf" and a draft MAP.

Proposed next steps
- Marcus to send two sizing options (conservative vs burst-optimized) by EOD Tue.
- Acme to confirm sustained vs burst split and any hard SLAs for streaming.
- We set a 1-week pilot with telemetry + synthetic traffic run to validate tail latency.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx (stated)

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + SLO targets from today

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from ops so Marcus can size appropriately: 

1) Concurrency breakdown: the 120 number is a peak sustained floor for daytime traffic (i.e., we regularly see 90–120 sustained concurrent non-streaming requests). Bursts (marketing push) can push short-lived concurrency to ~400 for 5–15 minutes.
2) Streaming profile: most streaming sessions are long-lived (2–20 minutes) but very low token-rate (~2–4 tokens/sec). We care more about tail latency while streaming (chunk delivery <= 200ms p99).
3) TLS/Connections: we will be using HTTP/2 where supported; connection re-use and keep-alive behavior will be important because our client pools are small (we prefer 6–10 backend sockets per app instance).
4) Heads up: holiday peak in Q4 has historically doubled concurrency numbers for ~2 weeks — need to plan headroom.

Please include guidance on per-api-key QPS limits and recommended connection-pool sizing in the proposal. Happy to take a short call if useful.

— Elena
Engineering Manager, Acme Corp
elena.ortiz@acme-corp.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + SLO targets from today

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks — this is helpful. Based on your profile (sustained daytime concurrency ~100, short bursts to ~400, streaming sessions with low token velocity) we recommend two concrete options so you can pick based on risk tolerance and budget: 

Option A — Dedicated performance pool (recommended for predictable p99)
- Provisioned dedicated pool sized for 150 sustained concurrency.
- Burst buffer capacity up to 450 concurrency for short durations (policy-based).
- Per-API-key soft QPS: 500 qps; hard cap 800 qps.
- Token budget: provisioned baseline 1.2M tokens/day, bursting allowed within pool limits.
- SLOs: 99th token generation latency target <= 200–250ms for <80 tokens; streaming chunk p99 <= 200ms.
- Network: HTTP/2 + TLS with recommended keep-alive and socket pool of 8 per client instance (we find 6–10 is ideal).

Option B — Cost-optimized + managed fallback (lower base cost)
- Baseline shared capacity sized for 80 sustained concurrency; automatic burst routing to supplementary nodes up to 220 concurrency.
- Per-API-key soft QPS: 300 qps; hard cap 500 qps.
- Token budget: ~750k tokens/day baseline with burst headroom.
- SLOs: best-effort p99 <= 300ms; guaranteed p95 <= 220ms. Streaming p99 target ~250ms.
- Network: recommend HTTP/2 multiplexing; if client pools are small, enable connection affinity to reduce TLS handshake overhead.

Practical suggestions and rollout
- Canary: a 7-day pilot with synthetic load that mimics both sustained and burst patterns (we run a red-team script to emulate holiday peak).
- Instrumentation: we'll provide trace headers and integration with your Datadog/Splunk. We'll look at tail latency, KV cache hit rates, and prefix reuse.
- Fallbacks: we can pre-configure a smaller model variant for graceful degradation if p99 spikes.

Please let us know which option you prefer and any hard constraints (e.g., absolute p99 ceilings, burst length > 15 minutes, contractual penalties for missed SLOs). If you prefer, Ben can follow up on commercial pricing for either option.

— Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + SLO targets from today

Elena / Tom —

Appreciate the quick internal sync. We discussed pricing and risk internally and Acme's profile maps best to a modified Option B with an expanded burst buffer. Summary of agreed items to put in the commercial amendment: 

Agreed (initial)
- Baseline: shared pool tuned for 90 sustained concurrency.
- Burst buffer: automatic burst to 300 concurrency for up to 20 minutes per occurrence (protects marketing pushes).
- Per-API-key soft QPS: 350 qps; hard cap 600 qps.
- Token budget: baseline 900k tokens/day with burst headroom within pool limits.
- Streaming: keep streaming p99 <= 225ms; client should enable HTTP/2 and 8 sockets per app instance where possible.
- Canary: 7-day pilot scheduled start 2026-11-22 (redwood will run synthetic holiday-like ramp).

Next steps
- Ben: send commercial amendment and payment terms; target signature to enable pilot.
- Legal/Proc (Acme): review amendment for burst window and penalty language.
- Marcus: prepare pilot runbook and telemetry dashboard links.

I'll attach the MAP and the connection-playbook to the HubSpot record and loop Legal once Ben shares the amendment. Thanks everyone — excited to get the pilot started.

--
Laura Bennett
